text:
### Observed differences

- Routing out of A36 changed: in the earlier window, about 97 in 100 of A36's outgoing transitions went to A25, with A30 not observed among its successors; in the later window, about 70 in 100 go to A30 and only about 28 in 100 to A25. A36's outgoing transitions also rose from about 1 to about 3.5 per trace, while A36 itself appears in every trace in both windows. [DIR001, POS003]
- The fixed sequence among A14, A30 and A36 dissolved: earlier, A14 preceded A30 in about 99 in 100 traces, A14 preceded A36 in about 99, and A30 preceded A36 in about 98, with all three activities co-occurring in every trace; in the later window only about 32 in 100 keep each of these orders, and about 68 in 100 show the pairs interleaved or repeated, with co-occurrence still at 100 in 100. [REL003, REL004, REL005]
- The close adjacency of A30 and A36 largely disappeared: earlier, the ordered pair A30 then A36 sat two steps apart in about 98 in 100 traces; in the later window only about 17 in 100 of these ordered pairs fall within five steps, the rest lying farther apart. [LAG002]
- Positions became more variable: A30 and A36 occur slightly later on average (relative position about 0.41 to 0.44 and 0.48 to 0.49) with roughly twice the spread (about 0.07 to 0.12); A14 drifts slightly earlier (about 0.14 to 0.12). [POS001, POS002, POS003]
- A05's involvement loosened: it still co-occurs with A30/A36 in about half of traces (about 54 in 100 before, 52 in 100 after), but A05 preceding them fell from about 54 in 100 to about 16 in 100, replaced mostly by interleaving (about 35 in 100); the gap from A05 to A14 widened from typically one to two steps to typically two to three. [REL001, REL002, LAG001]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the possibility that, in the later window, the segment around A30 and A36 runs as a repeated cycle instead of a single fixed pass: A36 recurs about three to four times per trace instead of about once, its flow returns to A30 in about 70 in 100 transitions rather than proceeding to A25, and the previously near-universal order A14 then A30 then A36 survives in only about a third of traces, with the A30-to-A36 adjacency typically stretched beyond five steps. This is shown directly by the successor change at A36, by the same order dissolution across all three pairs among A14, A30 and A36 at unchanged full co-occurrence, and by the collapse of the two-step A30–A36 adjacency; eleven items qualified where about 0.28 were expected for an unchanged process (all control-flow), and every item's difference exceeds those in about 995 of 1000 random re-splits. [DIR001, REL003, REL004, REL005, LAG002, POS002, POS003]

The evidence cannot pin down the exact shape of the cycle: the relation indicator merges traces where both orders occur with traces where activities repeat, so it cannot say whether A30, A36 or both repeat, nor whether A14 still precedes the cycle in the interleaved traces; it also does not show whether A25 now follows later by another route or is reached less often, since A25's overall participation is not reported. All positional and gap evidence uses event positions, not clock time. [REL003, REL004, REL005, DIR001]

Other differences: A05's ordering with A30 and A36 loosened in the same direction (A05 first fell from about 54 in 100 to about 16 in 100, interleaving rose to about 35 in 100) while its participation stayed near half of traces, the A05-to-A14 gap widened by about one step, and A14's mean relative position moved slightly earlier; these fit the same loosening of the sequence but are not needed for the main hypothesis. [REL001, REL002, LAG001, POS001]
